text:
maya (Marketing): Quick brainstorm — we need a tight latency vs cost narrative for the benchmark launch. Thinking of splitting into three short visuals:
- one showing median vs tail latency across model variants (SLO tiers),
- one showing $/1k tokens by quantization + batching config,
- one showing 'real app throughput' (requests/min) vs monthly cost for 3 archetypes (chat, summarization, search).
Which of these would land best on the landing page + tweet thread + webinar slide?

sam (Data Viz): I like the 3-chart approach. For the first chart can we show both median and 95th with shading? helps convey tail risk.

owen (Growth): +1. Also suggest a single composite KPI callout: "$ per 1k tokens at 99ms median" — something snappy for ads.

maya (Marketing): Good call, @owen. Need variants for PLG vs enterprise audiences. PLG sees the cheap quantized numbers, enterprise wants predictability/SLA view.

tara (Content): For copy: short hero line — "Serve LLMs at predictable latency and half the unit cost" then subline: "Real-world benchmarks across configs — pick the latency or price point that fits your product." Thoughts?

sam (Data Viz): For the cost chart, prefer log-scale on y to compress extremes, but add axis ticks and an explanatory note. Also show sample configs in a small legend: FP16, 8-bit, 4-bit + KV cache enabled.

owen (Growth): Routing note: CTA split — "Try hosted API" vs "Book dedicated trial". On the landing page, route people who click cost-focused CTAs to PLG signup; SLA-focused CTAs go to an enterprise form. We can gateby URL param.

maya (Marketing): Good — can we add UTM tags for each CTA? We'll map inbound routing in HubSpot. @owen can you sketch routing rules?

owen (Growth): Sure. Rule sketch:
- cost-cta -> /signup?utm=bench_cost -> PLG flow
- sla-cta -> /enterprise/interest?utm=bench_enterprise -> AE queue + dedicated demo routing
- webinar-cta -> /webinar?utm=bench_webinar -> nurture sequence
I'll set up initial lists.

bench-bot: benchmark-run-2026-03-12 finished. Attached CSV: /s3/bench-2026-03-12.csv (sample metrics: median_latency_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_sec, usd_per_1k_tokens).

sam (Data Viz): Nice. I'll pull sample rows and draft charts tomorrow. Quick ask: can we include a tiny table under the cost chart with "typical config used" so engineers can reproduce?

tara (Content): For the webinar: 20 min demo + 10 min Q&A. Title option: "Latency-first inference: hitting SLAs without breaking the bank". Another option: "Serving LLMs: predictable performance, controllable cost". Which tone do we want? technical or product?

maya (Marketing): Mix — start technical (bench highlights) then product examples. Need 3 quick customer-facing hooks we can A/B test in emails. Suggestions:
- Hook A: "Cut token cost by X% while keeping latency under Yms"
- Hook B: "Scale inference: predictable latency at lower unit cost"
- Hook C: "How we route and degrade gracefully so your app stays live"

owen (Growth): A/B test A vs B in email subject lines. C is better for enterprise nurture.

sam (Data Viz): Visual asks for design team:
1) small sparkline grid showing latency distribution by model variant,
2) bar + error bars for cost-per-1k tokens across quantized settings,
3) area chart for throughput vs monthly cost by archetype.
I'll add sample colors and axis labels in Figma comments.

tara (Content): Social copy: one threaded tweet that starts with the big number (e.g., "$0.XX per 1k tokens at 90ms median"), then 2 follow-ups: quick explainer and sign-up link. Keep it under 4 tweets.

maya (Marketing): Timeline: visuals by Wed EOD, copy + CTAs Thurs, landing + routing live Fri morning, webinar promo next week. Any blockers?

sam (Data Viz): No blockers on my side, will drop draft images by Wed.

owen (Growth): I'll prep the routing and UTMs today. Need final CTAs and form IDs.

tara (Content): I'll draft email + social variants after visuals land.

maya (Marketing): Great. Last ask: include one short FAQ blurb explaining quantization tradeoffs for non-ML readers. Keep it two lines.

sam (Data Viz): Draft FAQ: "Quantization reduces memory and cost by lowering numeric precision. In practice, we recommend validating quality on a 1000-prompt set — most chat use-cases are unaffected at 8-bit; 4-bit needs evals."

maya (Marketing): Perfect. Thanks all — will stitch into a 1-page brief for design + demand and drop in #design-ops. :thumbsup:

owen (Growth): :rocket:

bench-bot: pinned visual draft: /figma/bench-landing-draft (v1)
